query: How do I find a good first issue to work on?
expected_answer: Browse issues labeled "good first issue" (and "help wanted") in Kubernetes repositories such as kubernetes/kubernetes; for good first issues members commit to giving new contributors extra help. Other ways to start: improve documentation, help triage issues, write test coverage.

query: What do the lgtm and approved labels mean?
expected_answer: lgtm: prow adds this label after a reviewer comments /lgtm, meaning the code passed review. approved: prow adds it after approvers from each relevant OWNERS file comment /approve. A PR is merged automatically only with both labels and no blocking labels such as do-not-merge/hold.

query: How do I become a Kubernetes org member?
expected_answer: Requirements: two-factor authentication on GitHub, multiple contributions including at least one merged PR, subscription to dev@kubernetes.io, having read the contributor guide, active contribution to a subproject, and sponsorship by 2 reviewers from different companies who worked closely with you. Then open an issue against the kubernetes/org repo, mention the sponsors and complete the checklist; sponsors confirm with +1.

query: Which SIG is responsible for networking?
expected_answer: SIG Network. It owns pod networking (CNI), Services (including kube-proxy), Ingress, DNS and Network Policy; issues can be labeled with /sig network.

query: My PR has been open for two weeks, who should I ping?
expected_answer: Do not close and reopen the PR; ping your reviewers in a PR comment with @<github username>. If it still does not get enough attention, post a link to the PR in the #pr-reviews channel on Slack to find additional reviewers.

query: How do I report a Code of Conduct violation?
expected_answer: Email the Kubernetes Code of Conduct Committee at conduct@kubernetes.io. Do not report incidents in the public Slack channel; in urgent cases you may also contact committee members on Slack, but an email must still be sent.

query: Do I need to sign anything before my first pull request?
expected_answer: Yes, you must sign the CNCF Contributor License Agreement (CLA). After you open your first pull request, the linux-foundation-easycla bot posts your CLA status and a link to sign it (as an individual or corporate contributor).

query: How do I rerun tests that failed on my PR?
expected_answer: Comment /retest on the pull request to rerun the failed tests. Pushing new commits to the PR also re-triggers the tests automatically.

query: Why don't tests run automatically on my pull request?
expected_answer: If you are not a member of the Kubernetes organization, a member must first check your PR and comment /ok-to-test (the PR has the needs-ok-to-test label). Tests run automatically only for PRs from org members.

query: Where should I report a security vulnerability?
expected_answer: Report it privately by email to security@kubernetes.io (the Security Response Committee), including a proof of concept or a code trace. Reports are acknowledged within three working days.

query: How do I squash my commits before merging?
expected_answer: Use an interactive rebase (git rebase -i HEAD~<n>), change pick to squash for the commits to combine (fixes, typos, review feedback, work in progress), then force push the branch (git push --force or --force-with-lease). The bot can also squash commits via a label.

query: What should a good commit message look like?
expected_answer: Subject line of 50 characters or less (never over 72), capitalized, in imperative mood, without a final period; a blank line before the body; body wrapped at 72 characters and explaining what and why; no GitHub keywords or @mentions.

query: What is an OWNERS file?
expected_answer: OWNERS files are YAML files that assign responsibility for parts of the codebase. They list reviewers (who can /lgtm) and approvers (who can /approve), and may contain labels, options and emeritus_approvers; prow uses them in the two-phase code review.

query: What are the requirements to become a reviewer?
expected_answer: Be an org member for at least 3 months, be the primary reviewer for at least 5 PRs, have reviewed or merged at least 20 substantial PRs, know the codebase, and be sponsored by a subproject approver with no objections from other approvers; it is done through a PR that adds you to the reviewers in the OWNERS file.

query: What is a KEP and when do I need one?
expected_answer: A KEP is a Kubernetes Enhancement Proposal. You need one for a large or otherwise significant change, to confirm that the feature is wanted before implementing it; for small changes it is enough to discuss in an issue or the SIG's Slack channel.

query: How do I stop my PR from being merged too early?
expected_answer: Comment /hold on the PR (adds the do-not-merge/hold label) and /hold cancel when it is ready, or prefix the PR title with WIP.

query: How do I get my fix into an older Kubernetes release?
expected_answer: Cherry-pick it: after the fix is merged to master, run hack/cherry_pick_pull.sh upstream/release-X.Y <PR number> for each applicable release branch. Only security fixes, regression fixes, critical bug fixes and a few similar change types are eligible, and the release team's cherry-pick deadlines apply.

query: What rules should I follow in the Kubernetes Slack?
expected_answer: Keep conversations on topic and follow the Code of Conduct; join only through the community inviter; no spam or self-promotion, no unsolicited direct messages, no company business, no unapproved bots or apps; report violations with the Message Reporter.

query: Are there mentoring programs for new contributors?
expected_answer: Yes. The community runs mentoring initiatives such as group mentoring, Outreachy, Google Summer of Code (GSoC), Google Season of Docs and LFX Mentorship.

query: How do I label an issue as a bug?
expected_answer: Comment /kind bug on the issue (adds the kind/bug label), usually together with a SIG label such as /sig <name>.

query: What is the path from my first contributions to becoming a reviewer?
expected_answer: First become an org member: 2FA, multiple contributions with at least one merged PR, 2 sponsoring reviewers from different companies, an issue in kubernetes/org. Then, after at least 3 months as a member, be the primary reviewer for at least 5 PRs, review or merge at least 20 substantial PRs, get sponsored by a subproject approver and be added to the OWNERS file via a PR.

query: What is the difference between a reviewer and an approver?
expected_answer: Reviewers check code quality and correctness and signal it with /lgtm; approvers check holistic acceptance (compatibility, API and flag conventions, interactions with the system) and signal it with /approve. Approvers have stricter requirements: reviewer for at least 3 months, primary reviewer for at least 10 substantial PRs, at least 30 reviewed or merged PRs, nominated by a subproject owner.

query: What steps does a pull request go through from opening to merging?
expected_answer: Sign the CLA via EasyCLA; for non-members an org member comments /ok-to-test; automatic tests run (/retest for flakes); a reviewer adds /lgtm; approvers from the OWNERS files add /approve; with lgtm and approved labels, passing tests and no hold, Tide merges the PR automatically.

query: How is reporting a security vulnerability different from reporting a Code of Conduct violation?
expected_answer: Security vulnerabilities go privately to security@kubernetes.io (Security Response Committee) with a proof of concept; reports are acknowledged within three working days. Code of Conduct violations go to the Code of Conduct Committee at conduct@kubernetes.io, are handled confidentially and should not be reported in the public Slack channel.

query: How should I prepare my commits before my pull request is merged?
expected_answer: Squash fixes, typos, review feedback and work-in-progress commits with an interactive rebase and force push, so that every remaining commit is a meaningful unit of work; write commit messages with a short imperative subject (50 characters or less), a blank line and a body explaining what and why.

query: I am not an org member yet. What extra steps will my first pull request need?
expected_answer: You must sign the CLA (the EasyCLA bot posts a link after the first PR), and an org member has to check the PR and comment /ok-to-test before the tests run; for members tests run automatically.

query: Where can I talk to the community and what rules apply there?
expected_answer: Slack (e.g. #kubernetes-contributors), mailing lists such as dev@kubernetes.io, the discuss.kubernetes.io forum and Zoom community meetings. The Code of Conduct applies everywhere; on Slack conversations must stay on topic and spam, self-promotion and unsolicited direct messages are prohibited.
